name: Beothuk
confidence_why: Beothuk died out in 1829 and survives only in wordlists, and the two studies that examine the accent marks in those lists, Gatschet 1886 and Hewson 1978, both conclude that no stress rule can be drawn from them (Gatschet adds only that the marked accents are never final and often antepenultimate, and Hewson that the marks may show length rather than stress), while Howley 1915 merely reprints Gatschet and no source offers a rule.
catalog_citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1886. The Beothuk Indians. Second article. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 23(123): 411-432.
catalog_locator: pp. 418-419 (last paragraph of p. 418 continuing to the top of p. 419, in the section on sounds immediately before 'Alternation of sounds'; archive.org jstor-983225, saved)
catalog_quote: Too little information is on hand to establish any general rules for the accentuation. None of the accented words are oxytonized, but several have the antepenult emphasized: báshedtheek, áshwoging, dósomite; the term éjabathook has the accent still further removed from the final syllable. Very likely the accent could in that language shift, as in other languages of America, from syllable to syllable, whenever rhetorical reasons required it. By some of the collectors the signs for length and brevity were used to designate the emphasized syllable, placed above or underneath the vowels.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (23-page JSTOR Early Journal Content scan, text present; PDF pages 9-10 = printed pp. 418-419, running heads 'Gatschet.] 418 [May 7,' and '1886.] 419 [Gatschet.'). The quoted paragraph is the last paragraph of p. 418 continuing to the top of p. 419, exactly at the stated locator, inside the sounds section (consonant table, remarks on lth/dr/dth/x, gemination, syllable structure) that precedes 'Alternation of sounds'. Rendered p. 418 to PNG and read it: printed text is 'Too little information is on hand to establish any general rules for the accentuation [italic]. None of the accented words are oxytonized, but several have the antepenult emphasized : báshedtheek, áshwoging, dósomite;…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule can be stated: the only evidence is accent marks on a handful of wordlist items. In those, stress is never on the final syllable and is often on the antepenult (or earlier), but the source declines to generalize.
new_statements.exceptions: Gatschet suggests the accent could shift from syllable to syllable for rhetorical reasons, as he believed of other American languages; he also warns that some collectors used length/brevity signs to mark the emphasized syllable, so the marks are ambiguous between stress and vowel length (Hewson 1978: 115 makes the same point and drops the marks).
new_statements.domain_note: Written wordlist forms (single words in citation form) with accent marks added by 19th-century English-speaking collectors; Gatschet never heard the language. No phrase-level observations.
new_statements.identity_note: Beothuk is extinct (last speaker Shanawdithit d. 1829); all data are 18th-19th-century English-orthography wordlists from Oubee, Demasduwit and Shanawdithit, compiled by Gatschet (1885-1890) and re-edited by Hewson (1978). No dialect issue; no other glottocode involved.
